title: Salade Lyonnaise
subtitle: Frisee salad with bacon and poached egg
excerpt: Curly endive tossed in a warm bacon and sherry vinegar dressing, topped with a poached egg. A brasserie classic from Lyon that works as a starter or light lunch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salade lyonnaise is one of the signature dishes of Lyonnaise bouchon cooking. The warm bacon dressing wilting slightly bitter frisee with a poached egg on top is documented in Lyon-focused cookery writing from the early twentieth century.

content.text: Salade lyonnaise is a warm salad of frisee tossed in a dressing made from the bacon fat and sherry vinegar, topped with a freshly poached egg. When you cut into the egg the yolk runs into the dressing and coats the leaves. The flavour is sharp and rich at the same time, which is the whole point of the dish.
Bring a saucepan of water to a simmer. Add the white wine vinegar. Divide the frisee between two plates.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the bacon lardons for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp and golden. Do not drain the fat from the pan.
Meanwhile, poach the eggs in the barely simmering water for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain briefly on kitchen paper.
Remove the bacon pan from the heat. Stir the sherry vinegar and mustard into the hot fat and stir together quickly. Pour the warm dressing and bacon over the frisee and toss to wilt slightly.
Top each salad with a poached egg. Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately.
